mike: quick FYI — I ran into a puzzling behavior in the Go generator sample: cancelling the caller ctx during the initial HTTP/2 handshake sometimes leaves the consumer goroutine stuck on Events(). Thought I'd share repro and proposed fix.

mike: repro (very small):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
gen := client.Generator(ctx, opts)
go func() { for ev := range gen.Events() { _ = ev } }()
// cancel right after start
cancel()
// sometimes app still hangs for a few seconds
```

mike: investigating showed two problems: (1) auth refresh helper spun a background goroutine with its own ctx.Background() and held a ref to transport; (2) read loop blocked on decoder.ReadToken() without selecting on ctx.Done().

sophie: nice root cause. For (1) we should switch refresh/retry helpers to errgroup.WithContext so they inherit cancellation. For (2) adding a select on g.ctx.Done() before blocking read will let us bail early.

dan: another small change: ensure we call req = req.WithContext(g.ctx) immediately before RoundTrip so middleware can't accidentally strip request context. Also expose Generator.Close() that calls cancel() and closes Events channel — doc it as "defer gen.Close()" pattern.

mike: implemented a tiny patch that: uses errgroup, sets request ctx just before RoundTrip, and changes read loop to check ctx.Done(). Local sampleapp and CI e2e no longer show lingering goroutines. Branch: go-gen-cancel-fix-2026.

build-bot: CI started for go-gen-cancel-fix-2026 (build #4622).

sophie: please add a short note in sampleapp README about cancelling vs Close(), and a one-liner in migration docs so existing users know about Close(). Also add a small unit/integration that cancels mid-handshake and asserts the process exits quickly (avoid flaky NumGoroutine checks).

dan: will also audit other SDKs for parity (JS/Py) and open a cross-sdk issue to keep behavior consistent.

mike: thanks — should make onboarding less confusing ("app never exits" bug). I'll leave the minimal repro in PR description for reviewers.
